content: 1. Pexidartinib and UGT Inhibitors: If the concurrent use of UGT inhibitors with pexidartinib cannot be avoided, the dose of pexidartinib should be reduced. After discontinuing the UGT inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the original pexidartinib dose may be resumed. 2. Cobicistat and Pexidartinib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the original dose may be resumed. 3. Phenobarbital and Cobicistat: Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If necessary, monitor for a lack of virologic response. 4. Phenytoin and Cobicistat: Phenytoin reduces cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If necessary, monitor for virologic response loss. 5. Cobicistat and Pimavanserin: Cobicistat increases pimavanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day. 6. Atazanavir and Pimavanserin: Atazanavir increases pimavanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Reduce the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 7. Cobicistat and Pirtobrutinib: Cobicistat increases pirtobrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib during the use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the original dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for five half-lives. 8. Atazanavir and Pirtobrutinib: Atazanavir increases pirtobrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib during the use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the original dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for five half-lives. 9. Atazanavir and Pomalidomide: Atazanavir increases pomalidomide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Cobicistat and Ponatinib: Cobicistat increases ponatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the starting dose of ponatinib to 30 mg daily. 11. Atazanavir and Ponatinib: Atazanavir increases ponatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the starting dose of ponatinib to 30 mg daily. 12. Posaconazole and Cobicistat: Posaconazole increases cobicistat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Atazanavir and Pralsetinib: Atazanavir increases pralsetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Cobicistat and Pralsetinib: Cobicistat increases pralsetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Primidone and Cobicistat: Primidone decreases cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 16. Atazanavir and Quetiapine: Atazanavir increases quetiapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the quetiapine dose to one-sixth of the current dose and monitor for adverse reactions. 17. Cobicistat and Quetiapine: Cobicistat increases quetiapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the quetiapine dose to one-sixth of the current dose and monitor for adverse reactions. 18. Rabeprazole and Atazanavir: Rabeprazole decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH, which reduces atazanavir solubility. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, limit the proton pump inhibitor (PPI) dose to an equivalent of omeprazole 20 mg and administer it approximately 12 hours before atazanavir/ritonavir in treatment-naïve patients. PPIs are not recommended in treatment-experienced patients taking atazanavir. 19. Atazanavir and Ranolazine: Atazanavir increases ranolazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 20. Atazanavir and Red Yeast Rice: Atazanavir increases red yeast rice levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Red yeast rice contains monacolin K, which is chemically identical to lovastatin, and may increase the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. 21. Cobicistat and Repotrectinib: Cobicistat increases repotrectinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors and wait 3–5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 22. Atazanavir and Resmetirom: Atazanavir increases resmetirom levels by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Cobicistat and Resmetirom: Cobicistat increases resmetirom levels by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Cobicistat and Ribociclib: Cobicistat increases ribociclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Atazanavir and Ribociclib: Atazanavir increases ribociclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Rifampin and Atazanavir: Rifampin decreases atazanavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 27. Rifapentine and Cobicistat: Rifapentine decreases cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 28. Rifapentine and Atazanavir: Rifapentine decreases atazanavir levels by inducing metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 29. Cobicistat and Rimegepant: Cobicistat increases rimegepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 30. Atazanavir and Rimegepant: Atazanavir increases rimegepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
